title.narrative: Life-saving emergency primary health care services for drought affected rural communities in Baidoa district.

description.narrative: ltpgtACF proposes an 8-month integrated emergency health response in Baidoa rural, addressing critical health service gaps exacerbated by recurrent drought, displacement, disease outbreaks, and the 2025 health funding contraction. Baidoa remains among Somalia’s most crisis-affected districts, hosting large IDP populations, marginalized ethnic minorities, and persons with disabilities facing persistent barriers to life-saving health services. The scale-down and closure of health facilities have significantly reduced access to preventive and curative care, increasing risks of maternal and child morbidity and mortality. The proposed project will provide integrated primary health care to 46,688 (23,344 W, 10,296 G, 4,120 M and 8,928 B) through three health centers (Tier 2 facility under the EPHS) namely Salbuuy, Boonkey and Meegaagle, linked with outreach services 2-3 days per week and complemented by iCCM in access constrained locations. Services will align with EPHS, WHO, and MoH protocols and include OPD consultations, routine immunization, ANC/PNC, skilled deliveries, BEmONC referrals, communicable disease management, MHPSS, and emergency referrals to secondary care. While ACF will directly implement the project due to its technical complexity and strong operational presence in Baidoa, the action advances localization through recruitment of qualified local health staff, collaboration with CHWs, and system-level integration with national health structures. Capacity strengthening will be delivered through on-the-job mentoring, refresher trainings, and supportive supervision. CHWs drawn from target communities, including marginalized groups, will support iCCM, health education, immunization follow-up, defaulter tracing, and referrals. Accountability to Affected Populations is ensured through ACF’s toll-free 3-digit hotline, multilingual IEC materials, and community consultations. Client satisfaction surveys, focus group discussions, and community review meetings will inform adaptive management. Community engagement under this project will apply a community-first approach to health service delivery, positioning communities as active partners in improving access to care. Building on Action Against Hunger’s Humanitarian Access Initiative (HAI) learning, we will first understand local health-seeking behaviours, trusted health actors, community coordination practices, and how communities gain access to services in constrained rural settings. Facilitated community dialogue will inform health priorities, identify barriers to care, and ensure inclusion of women, minority clans, youth, persons with disabilities, IDPs, and other excluded groups. For outreach health service delivery, communities will directly shape outreach by identifying priority populations, safe and acceptable service points, and co-planning outreach schedules aligned with local movement patterns, seasonality, and security dynamics. In outbreak-prone areas, CHWs will support early detection, referrals, and community-led risk reduction. 3% of the budget supports disability inclusion, and collaboration with the Alla Magan Southwest Association of the Disabled. ACF will coordinate closely with MoH, clusters, and RA partners to ensure intersectoral convergence (See comments under location tab). Strong risk mitigation, supply chain systems, safeguarding measures, and joint monitoring with authorities will ensure quality and continuity. The project will complement ACF’s ongoing support in the district by building on existing referral pathways established under the Damal Caafimaad and Caafimaad Plus programs, particularly for the referral of complicated cases to secondary-level health facilities. Through this action, ACF aims to reduce preventable maternal and child deaths, mitigate protection risks, and uphold dignity and equitable access to health services for the most vulnerable populations in Baidoa District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
